Where the score comes from

A MusicXML transcription from the PDMX collection (MuseScore users' scores), converted to ABC with xml2abc and checked note for note against the MusicXML: all 312 bars of every voice line up and every note's pitch and length agree.

Things to know about this transcription

  • The transcription had two oboe staves that agree in 260 of 312 bars; Mozart revised the oboe parts when he added clarinets. The one kept is the staff the transcriber set beside the clarinets, and the one with fewer notes, so probably the revised parts. Not yet checked against a printed edition.
  • Cello and bass share a staff, as in Mozart's score. The bass is drawn only in the 14 bars where it plays something other than the cello an octave lower, and is heard throughout.
  • The transcriber hid a slowing-down in the last two bars (hidden notes and tempo changes). The page leaves them out and plays at one tempo.
  • Three horn passages in bass clef are drawn without the small 8 on the clef, so the browser plays them at the right pitch.

What playback leaves out

  • Each instrument is a set of single-loudness samples (the MusyngKite soundfont), one player per staff, with dynamics as loudness only.
  • Both halves are repeated, as the repeat signs say. Staccato dots and accents are drawn but the player does nothing special with them (not checked by ear).
